Lewis Hamilton Claims Ferrari Pole at Mexican Grand Prix as Antonelli Closes on F1 Title

01 Nov 2026, 06:15 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

Qualifying Highlights from Mexico City

At the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton secured his first pole position for Ferrari and the 105th of his Formula One career. According to reports from the qualifying session, Hamilton edged out Mercedes driver George Russell by just nine-thousandths of a second to claim the top spot.

  • Lewis Hamilton: First pole for Ferrari, his first since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix.
  • George Russell: Qualified second for Mercedes, locking out the front row alongside Hamilton.
  • Kimi Antonelli: Qualified in fourth place and remains well-positioned to secure his maiden world championship.

Championship Scenarios for Sunday

Young driver Kimi Antonelli enters Sunday's race needing to maintain a 100-point advantage over his closest rivals to clinch the world title. Currently leading Russell by 123 points and Hamilton by 124 points, the Italian driver can secure the championship under several conditions:

  • If Antonelli finishes in ninth place or higher, he claims the title regardless of where Russell or Hamilton finish.
  • Even if Antonelli fails to finish the race, he will still be champion unless either Russell or Hamilton wins the Grand Prix.

Grid Penalties and Notable Performances

Charles Leclerc qualified third for Ferrari, while Max Verstappen originally finished fourth on track but faces a one-place grid penalty stemming from a practice clash with Liam Lawson. Lawson also received a one-place penalty, and Lando Norris qualified sixth for McLaren. Further down the grid, Oscar Piastri suffered an early exit in Q2, finishing 13th due to a lack of rear grip.

Haas Team Changes and Esteban Ocon Statement

In separate paddock news, the Haas F1 Team announced that Esteban Ocon was replaced for the remainder of the race weekend by Ryo Hirakawa, who is set to make his F1 race debut. Haas provided no official explanation for the driver change.

Following media speculation regarding the sudden substitution, Ocon released a statement acknowledging a "difference in viewpoints" that led to discussions with team staff. However, Ocon categorically denied any reports suggesting physical violence occurred during the disagreement.

How to Verify

Readers can verify official qualifying results, grid lineups, and race updates by visiting the official Formula One website (formula1.com) or checking governing body announcements from the FIA.
